text: Thank you for that history. To better understand your weakness and decreased sensation in the right arm, could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they occurred gradually or suddenly? Also, have you noticed any neck pain or stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant weight loss, alcohol use, and steroid history, have you experienced any numbness or tingling in your hands at night, and do you have any difficulty with buttoning shirts or holding a glass? REQUEST TEST: TSH, Vitamin B12, and CBC; REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, and given your history of anabolic steroid use and heavy lifting, combined with the focal weakness and sensory loss, this strongly suggests a cervical radiculopathy or a compressive myelopathy rather than a systemic metabolic issue. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Right C5-C6 Radiculopathy.
